title: Calling eqx.Module method invokes user defined __getattr__
author: yuzu-ido

comments.author: patrick-kidger
comments.body:
So as a general Python thing (unrelated to JAX or Equinox) it's usually inadvisible to have a wildcard `__getattr__` that attempts to handle everything. It's pretty common for any code you interact with try to try doing something like:
```python
if hasattr(your_obj, "__some_magic_method__"):
    your_obj.__some_magic_method__(...)
```
which will give unexpected behaviour here!

In this case you're running afoul of exactly this kind of thing in Equinox: we check for `__name__` and `__qualname__` attributes at various points internally (along with several other special attributes) to be sure that we can forward them appropriately e.g. across flattening+unflattening.

The best fix here would be to check the value of `name` in your `__getattr__`, and only handle the ones you know you want to handle.

An alternative would be to handle this case in particular by doing:
```python
if name in ("__name__", "__qualname__"):
    raise AttributeError
```

comments.author: yuzu-ido
comments.body: Thanks for the response. There's quite a lot of `name` I'd want to handle, so the alternative option sounds like a plan. My temporary fix was to copy and paste the ~10 line helper function into` __getattr__` directly but that seems cleaner.
